headline: RWE's chief executive argues that data centres and other new power users should help pay for Europe's grid expansion.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: an executive's interview; an opinion and a call for policy, not a decision.
importance_line: It matters to households and businesses who pay grid fees on their bills, and to data centre operators, who could pay more under this approach, but it is one company's view and no policy has been decided.
summary: Bloomberg reports, from an interview with Markus Krebber, chief executive of the German power company RWE, that Europe needs bigger grids and that firms creating extra power demand are not paying for the grid it requires. Krebber argues policymakers should consider directing grid costs to the sources of new demand, such as data centres, instead of spreading them across all customers.
